To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
position-induced differences in promoter activity are a complex phenomenon that can be characterized in detail by the use of a reporter gene system.

position-induced quantitative differences are probably the result of differences in spatial regulation of transgene expression, and that these differences in spatial regulation are inherited by the offspring.
the position-induced differences in expression of transgenes are caused by spatial and temporal changes of the transgene promoter activity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization and inheritance of spatial and temporal regulation patterns of transgene promoter activities in plants.
the characterization of spatial and temporal position effects on transgene promoter activity and their consequences for transgene expression in Arabidopsis thalia.

the characterization of position-induced spatial regulation of transgene activity in plants, and the contribution of position-induced spatial variation to the observed position effect on transgene expression.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the expression of a transgene is a function of the promoter, the integration site and the developmental stage.
position-induced differences in gene expression are the result of differences in the local environment and/or local cell-type specific differences in gene expression.
position effect is a complex phenomenon, and that it is a combination of spatial and temporal effects.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the position effect of a transgene is a result of both the position effect of the promoter and the position effect of its transcription factors.
position effects are a complex phenomenon, which is a result of the interaction of different factors, including the transgene itself and the plant genotype.
position effects are not just due to differences in the integration site, but are also due to spatial and temporal differences in transgene promoter activation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
transgene expression is not only regulated by the transgene itself, but also by the plant in which it is inserted.
position effect can be a result of differences in spatial or temporal regulation of transgenic promoter activity.
transgene expression is not a simple on/off switch.
